newsitem.title: USA: U.S. farm trade surplus $1.620 billion in March.
newsitem.headline: U.S. farm trade surplus $1.620 billion in March.

text.p: The U.S. trade surplus in agricultural commodities was $1.620 billion in March, down from $2.068 billion in February, the Commerce Department said Wednesday.

In its monthly trade report, Commerce pegged farm exports at $4.820 billion in March, almost the same as February's $4.830 billion. Imports surged to $3.200 billion in March, up from $2.762 billion the preceding month.
Soybean exports plunged to $562 million, down $269 million. Wheat dipped slightly to $254 million. Corn rose to $568 million, up $46 million. Cotton was up $37 million to total $318 million.

Imports of coffee totaled $331 million, up $57 million, and fruit and vegetable imports leapt to $867 million, up $161 million. Vegetable oil and fat imports were up $25 million to $132 million. Sugar and tobacco imports declined slightly.
